parts.note: DI, short for Diana, a crossword princess, with the possessive S

explanation.walkthrough: DI'S LODGE would be one of the princess's residences (the answer to 14), so 'one of' tells you to take a single example of 14.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to shift or remove it from its position.

clue.text: Climbing released oxygen etc from the chase

O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
and the rest is what etc stands for

explanation.surface: Freed oxygen and so on rise up from the hunting ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A chase is an unenclosed hunting ground, the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A chase is open land kept for hunting, like a Scottish deer forest.

clue.text: Main problem among a succession of schools

indicators.note: the reordered letters sit within the succession

explanation.surface: The main problem among a run of schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' reworks MAIN into MINA, set among SERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminaries are colleges, especially for training priests, so they are schools.

clue.text: Question, when between 8s, the last part of one

definitions.text: Question, when between 8s, the last part of one

parts.words: Question, when between 8s, the last part of one
parts.note: 8 down gives two words; placed between two copies of them this makes Hamlet's famous question, and alone it ends any yes-or-no question

explanation.surface: A riddle about what goes between two copies of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is TO BE; Hamlet asks 'To be or not to be'. Tacked onto a question ('Coming, or not?') the phrase is its last part.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's question puts this phrase between two copies of 'to be', and it often closes a question.

definitions.meaning: to bring about, a verb sense
what follows from a cause, its result

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to bring about; as a noun it is the result that follows a cause.

clue.text: Draft sure to be composed by a crook

indicators.note: the letters are to be put together afresh, composed into a new order

explanation.surface: A draft written with confidence by a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudster is a swindler, someone dishonest, which is a crook.

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An old volume, the final one in its era.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, so an old book.

explanation.surface: A demon has been let loose somewhere unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the postal abbreviation for Alberta, the Canadian province whose capital this city is.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the Canadian province of Alberta, abbreviated AB, so it lies in AB.

clue.text: Capital of South Africa with water bird (detail)

parts.note: ZA is the international vehicle code for South Africa

indicators.note: read as de-tail: cut off the tail, the final letter of the bird

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.walkthrough: '(detail)' looks like a bracketed aside but reads as de-tail, removing the last E of GREBE to leave GREB.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Discover about energy, also the type of opening to 13

indicators.note: the word for discover goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to discover is to find
E is the physics symbol for energy
too means also

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about discovering energy and some kind of opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening of 13 (COMBINABLE) is COMB, and a comb with close teeth is the type meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb with closely set teeth is described by this compound adjective, so it names a type of comb.

clue.text: Bambi clone could be other than oil and water

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A cloned Bambi might be something that mixes, unlike oil and water.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil and water famously do not mix, so anything other than them can be mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil and water cannot be combined; things unlike them are capable of joining together.

indicators.note: the letters revolve into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary has been vetted for a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarters are lodgings, places where people live, as are residences.

clue.text: Gatherings of rugby players abandon situations in the country

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, the players' code

indicators.note: the gatherings drop the letters for situations, leaving what remains

parts.note: rallies are mass gatherings
a lie is a situation or position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: Groups of rugby players leave their positions out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandon' takes the situations out of the gatherings; a lie, as in a golf ball's lie, is its situation or position.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rural belongs to or is found in the countryside.

clue.text: Tearful priest keeps church line to the left

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A weeping clergyman keeps the church on the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is a crossword abbreviation for railway, hence line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal means relating to tears, so weepy or tearful.

clue.text: One coming out with it — with some money I say's gone out

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, makes her coming-out into society
a bank note is some money

explanation.surface: A debutante makes her entrance, mentioning that cash has been spent.
explanation.walkthrough: The document itself speaks: it says that money has gone out of an account. 'Coming out' is a debutante's first appearance in society, a British upper-class custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial document recording a sum charged to an account says that money is going out.

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect the prison's fundamental components.
explanation.definitionFit: These undifferentiated biological units can develop into other types, so they are basic building blocks of the body.

explanation.walkthrough: The scut belongs to a RABBIT; with the scut gone, so is the tail end, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and minister of a congregation.

clue.text: Revival concerned with article in car establishment

clue.text: Return of colleague about 1BC constituting a single sound

parts.note: of a colleague is an ally's

indicators.note: BC is placed around the numeral

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone returns with a colleague, around the year 1 BC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of colleague' stands for the possessive, an ally's; 'Return' turns that round, and 'about' puts the date's letters around the Roman numeral for 1.

definitions.meaning: the gurgling noise a turkey makes, its talk

explanation.surface: Should one eat a turkey or speak frankly with it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk turkey' is an idiom for speaking frankly, but here it is the noise a turkey makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to eat greedily and to make a turkey's throaty call.

definitions.meaning: of a sky with cloud cover hiding the stars
lacking stars, read literally as the answer

explanation.surface: A gloomy night sky and a party with no famous guests.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast night sky shows no stars, and a show with no famous names has no stars either.
